questions.question: Which browser rendering stage is triggered when animating the width or margin of an element?
questions.explanation: Changing dimensions (width, height, margin) triggers the Layout (Reflow) stage, which recalculates the geometry of elements on the page.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of the modern CSS property content-visibility: auto?
options: It skips rendering off-screen elements until the user scrolls near them, speeding up initial page load by up to 70%
questions.explanation: content-visibility: auto defers rendering work for off-screen content until it is about to enter the viewport.

questions.question: Why is CSS considered a 'render-blocking' resource by browsers?
options: Browsers refuse to parse HTML if CSS exists
The browser will not draw any pixels to screen until external CSS is downloaded and the CSSOM is constructed
CSS is only processed after JavaScript finishes
questions.hint: Blocks painting pixels until styles are parsed.
questions.explanation: To prevent Flash of Unstyled Content (FOUC), browsers block page rendering until stylesheets are parsed into the CSSOM.

questions.question: Why should will-change be used sparingly rather than applied globally?
options: Excessive will-change forces the browser to allocate dedicated GPU memory layers, which can exhaust device RAM
questions.hint: Excessive GPU layer creation consumes device memory.
questions.explanation: will-change allocates dedicated GPU memory buffers; overusing it consumes massive device memory and degrades performance.

questions.question: Which two CSS properties bypass both the Layout and Paint stages during animation?
questions.explanation: transform and opacity are composited directly on the GPU, completely bypassing expensive Layout and Paint stages.
